title: How early should you arrive at Exeter Airport?
author: Matt
cover_image_alt: A passenger jet coming in to land at sunset, silhouetted against an orange sky
intro: Exeter is a small, one-terminal airport, so about two hours before a holiday flight is usually plenty, and less for a short domestic hop. Here's how much time to allow, the liquids rule and how to get there.
seo_description: About 2 hours before a holiday flight from Exeter, 1½ hours for a domestic flight with hand luggage, and more at peak times. Liquids, bus 56 and parking.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Domestic, hand luggage:** about 1½ hours
- **Holiday flights with bags:** about 2 hours
- **Early morning waves:** add 30 mins
- **Liquids:** 100ml, in a clear bag

These are our suggestions, not airport rules. The deadlines that matter are your airline's check-in and bag drop times, which are in your booking. Rules change, so check with the airport or your airline before you fly. We checked the details below in November 2026.

sections.heading: Why Exeter is usually quick
sections.text:
Exeter is a small regional airport with one terminal and a short walk from check-in to security to the gates. On a normal day, queues are short.

The busy times are the early morning waves of holiday flights, especially on summer Saturdays and around school holidays, when several TUI and Ryanair flights leave close together. If your flight is in that first wave, allow the extra half an hour.

sections.heading: How early for your flight
sections.text:
| Flight | Who flies it | Our suggestion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domestic and Channel Islands | Loganair | 1½ hours, or 1 hour with hand luggage only |
| Dublin and Amsterdam | Irish and Dutch airlines | 2 hours |
| Summer and winter sun | TUI and Ryanair | 2 hours, 2½ at busy times |

TUI is the biggest airline at Exeter, and its package holiday flights mean a lot of people dropping bags at once. If you've checked in online with hand luggage only, you can go straight to security.

Tip: Ryanair's bag drop closes 40 minutes before departure, and many other airlines close check-in 40 to 60 minutes before. Missing it means missing the flight, even if you're in the terminal.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
When we checked, Exeter's own guidance said there were no changes to the liquids rules. So plan on the standard rule:

- **Liquids:** containers of 100ml or less, in a single clear resealable bag of about 1 litre.
- **Electronics:** be ready to take laptops and tablets out of your bag.
- **Larger liquids:** pack them in your hold bag, or buy them after security.

Watch out: some UK airports now allow bigger containers or let you leave liquids in your bag, so the rules on your flight out and your flight home may differ. Check Exeter's website before you pack, in case its scanners have changed.

sections.heading: After security
sections.text:
Once you're airside, there's one departure lounge with a café, a bar and a duty-free shop, and the gates are a short walk away. Small airports don't always call flights loudly, so keep an eye on the departure screens.

Boarding usually starts 30 to 40 minutes before departure, and the gate closes about 15 to 20 minutes before, so don't wait for a final call. On the smaller propeller planes, bigger cabin bags may be taken from you at the aircraft steps and returned when you land, so keep medicines, chargers and valuables in a small bag.

sections.heading: Getting to Exeter Airport
sections.text:
The airport is about five miles east of Exeter, near junction 29 of the M5. There's no railway station at the airport itself.

- **By bus:** Stagecoach's service 56 links the airport with Exeter city centre and Exeter St Davids station, taking about 25 to 30 minutes. It runs less often on Sundays and bank holidays, so check the timetable for early flights.
- **By car:** the airport has short and long stay car parks, and booking ahead online is usually cheaper. Check the airport's website for drop-off arrangements and any charges.
- **By taxi:** about 15 to 20 minutes from the city centre, depending on traffic.

For a dawn departure, the first bus may not get you there in time, so most people drive, take a taxi or stay nearby the night before.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Exeter?
sections.text:
Exeter's routes are mostly holiday flights, with some city links:

- **Sun:** [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife), [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca) or the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve)
- **City breaks:** [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam), for a weekend or onward connections

Routes change every season, so check the airport's current destinations page before you plan. For more choice, [Bristol](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-bristol-airport) is about 1½ hours up the M5. If you can't agree where to go, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put your shortlist into a draw on somewhere.party.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Exeter Airport?
faqs.answer: About 2 hours before a holiday flight if you're dropping a bag, and 1½ hours for a domestic flight. Add 30 minutes for early morning flights and school holidays.

faqs.question: What is the liquids limit at Exeter Airport?
faqs.answer: When we checked, Exeter still used the standard rule: containers of 100ml or less in a clear 1-litre bag. Check the airport's website before you fly, in case this changes.

faqs.question: How do you get to Exeter Airport by public transport?
faqs.answer: Take Stagecoach bus 56 from Exeter St Davids station or the city centre. It takes about 25 to 30 minutes, with fewer buses on Sundays.

faqs.question: Is there a train station at Exeter Airport?
faqs.answer: No. The nearest mainline station is Exeter St Davids, linked to the airport by bus 56.
